measuredBy: Tropenmuseum second pass, 2026-10-14: read off the rectified panorama crops of landmark-brief.ts (artifacts/landmark-briefs/tropenmuseum/, Gemeente Amsterdam panoramas CC BY 4.0, 50 px/m) with the metre grid of elevation-grid.ts at 100 px/m. Values in `inferred` lists are not visible in any crop (tree, banner, sign or the crop edge).
frame: s = metres along the photographed wall from its viewer-left corner (the crop's left edge); y = metres above the 3DBAG ground (crop bottom row). On the builder's panel u = s + sToU (tropenmuseum-walls.ts prints the panels and offsets). Every y pair is [bottom, top] of the glazed opening; every s pair is [left, right].
pattern: Shared by the museum's three-bay pavilion faces (register: 'gebeeldhouwde friezen onder de vensters ... de vier voornaamste godsdiensten ... en landbouwcultures'): raised souterrain with round-arched barred windows, a stone string course, then per floor two single side windows (tall lower light with a ledge, short upper light with a corniced hood and a blind brick arch over it) and a centre triple window in two tiers; a relief slab under a dentil cornice between the floors under the centre; a wrought-iron anchor between the bays; a round-arched head over the top triple; a dentil cornice under the stage above.

inferred: dentil cornice at y 21.45-22.0: above the crop top (21.46); placed 0.45 m above w12's cornice because this crop's plinth is 0.45 m higher
centre triple surround widths and the ledge depths (0.1-0.12 m)
relief slab depth 0.06 m and its frame 0.1 m: shadows only
